inputs.original_text: In Paris, the conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, under France's new law against psychological subjection shows how religious institutions continue to exert coercive control over people. While this has stirred pushback from religious communities and civil liberties advocates who seem more focused on preserving traditional power structures, it represents a necessary step to shield vulnerable groups from the manipulative hierarchies that have long exploited inequality and dependency. These systems don't operate in isolation—they reflect deeper patterns of institutional dominance that progressive reforms must dismantle to protect individual autonomy.
inputs.modified_text: Hey, I just heard about this case in Paris where Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, got convicted under France's new law against psychological subjection. It really drives home how religious institutions keep enforcing coercive control on people, especially by preying on those trapped in inequality and dependency. The backlash from religious communities and civil liberties advocates just shows they're more invested in shielding old power structures than in protecting anyone. This conviction is a vital move to defend vulnerable groups from those manipulative hierarchies that have long fed off systemic dominance. These aren't isolated problems—they're tied to broader patterns of institutional oppression that we need to break down through real progressive reforms to finally secure individual autonomy.
